newsitem.title: DENMARK: Advantage for Denmark to join stable EMU - Wise Men.
newsitem.headline: Advantage for Denmark to join stable EMU - Wise Men.

text.p: The independent Danish Economic Council said in a report issued on Wednesday that it saw clear gains for Denmark in joining European Economic and Monetary Union, provided that the currency pact was stable.

"If EMU is stable, analyses show that there are considerable economic advantages in participating," the council, also known as the Wise Men, said in a statement published with its latest forecasts for the Danish economy.

"If there is a strong probability that monetary union is going to be stable and the risk of it sparking an economic shock which would specifically damage the Danish economy is deemed to be minimal, Denmark should not hesitate to join EMU from the start," the council said.
Denmark, which is already in Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM), satisfies EMU convergence criteria but its citizens voted in a binding 1993 referendum to stay out.
Although Danish industry and political leaders largely back membership, a reversal of the 1993 vote would require a fresh plebiscite, for which the government says it has no plans.
The Economic Council said that a main advantage to Denmark of staying outside EMU was that it would remain in control of its crown currency.
"An advantage to non-participation could be that Denmark would have the possibility of singlehandedly adjusting its currency if hit by a major domestic upheaval," it said.
